q: How do I check whether a company really has an SBTi-validated target?
title: Check if a company has an SBTi target
short: Search the company on the SBTi Target Dashboard at sciencebasedtargets.org. A validated target is listed with its wording, scopes and date. A commitment only means the company has promised to set one. Check the exact legal entity, because a parent's target may not cover the supplier you buy from.
audience: Buyers, lenders and suppliers checking claims

sections.h: Read the status, not the press release
ul: A validated target: the dashboard lists the target, its classification, the scopes it covers and its wording.
A commitment: the company has said it will set a target within the SBTi's deadline. Nothing is validated yet.
A commitment that was removed or has lapsed: treat any claim of an SBTi target as unsupported.
Not listed: no SBTi target or commitment under that name. Read the dashboard's own legend for the exact status labels.

ol: Match the legal name and country. Indian subsidiaries often trade under a group name that has a target.
Read the target text: near-term or net-zero, base year, target year, and which scopes it covers.
Check whether it was set on the SME route, and which scopes the entry lists.
Note the date; older targets may have been set under earlier criteria.
Ask for the company's latest published emissions and its progress against the target.

sections.h: Red flags in a supplier's claim
ul: A commitment presented as a validated target.
A parent company's target quoted for a separate legal entity without confirmation that it is included.
Credits presented as progress toward the target. The SBTi does not count credits as reductions.
